In East Newton, Surrey, the 55+ homes you can buy are Chelsea Gardens, Charleston Green and Sullivan Mews (strata and co-op or membership). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in East Newton
Chelsea Gardens — 13870 70 Ave and 13888 70 Ave (East Newton)

The largest verified 55+ ownership complex in the sub-area. Freehold strata, plan LMS1416, built 1995–1996, gated. MLS building data records "Restricted Age: 55+", adult-oriented / retirement community features, and pets allowed with restrictions; listings describe resort-style amenities — pool, hot tub, gym, workshop, library, English-style pub and clubhouse — within 23 acres of landscaping, paths and a pond. One building-data source records 395 homes; treat the unit count as UNCONFIRMED until checked against the strata plan, because the sources checked do not agree on a single plan-wide count.

Gated 55+ townhouse complex, freehold strata, plan NWS2625, built 1988. MLS property data for units in the complex records the sub-area as East Newton, the complex name as Charleston Green, and listings describe it as a "gated 55+ townhouse complex" with a clubhouse and pets allowed. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
55+ co-op and membership housing in East Newton (not strata)

MLS listings place this complex in the East Newton sub-area and describe a retirement community with a 55+ age restriction, a maximum of 2 occupants, no smoking and 1 small pet. It is NOT a strata: the listing states "This is not Strata. It is a membership therefore not mortgages possible" and that a purchase must be cash, with a monthly fee ($540 in the listing) covering taxes, heat, electricity, management, insurance and water. Do not market this as a strata condo or townhouse — the buyer purchases a membership, not a strata lot. Listing-stated figures — confirm against the membership documents before relying on them.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in East Newton (not for sale)

items.t: Arbourside Court — 13751 74 Ave (East Newton): Independent retirement living with supportive services, operating since 2001; its own site describes senior apartments (studio, one- and two-bedroom) with rents subject to change — this is a rental residence, not a building you buy into. Building sources place it in East Newton and describe it as geared to adults 65 and older, with meal-plan options, housekeeping, laundry and 24-hour staff. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED — building sources checked give conflicting counts (82 suites in one, 93 units in another).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around East Newton

items.t: East Newton is the Newton community land east of King George Boulevard, in the City of Surrey; the City's East Newton plan material is bounded by King George Highway to the west, 76 Avenue to the south, 152 Street to the east and Newton Athletic Park to the north.
King George Boulevard is the dividing street: West Newton is across it to the west, Panorama Ridge / Sullivan is south, and Fleetwood Tynehead is northeast.
The local pocket name inside East Newton is Chimney Hill, carried by Chimney Hill Elementary and Chimney Heights Park.
SD36 schools in the area: Chimney Hill Elementary, 14755 74 Ave; M.B.

Newton Athletic Park, 7395 128 St, sits at the north edge of the plan area; the Newton Recreation Centre and Newton branch of Surrey Libraries are at the 13795 70 Ave town-centre site, west of King George Boulevard.

Transit: the R1 RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard between Newton Exchange and King George Station via Surrey Central Station; route 321 runs via 152 St and King George Blvd; route 324 runs via 132 St. No SkyTrain station is inside East Newton.
Health care: Surrey Memorial Hospital, 13750 96 Ave; Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 6830 King George Blvd.

Where the 55+ housing actually concentrates: one cluster on 70 Avenue just east of King George Boulevard (Chelsea Gardens at 13870 / 13888 70 Ave, Arbourside Court at 13751 74 Ave), one gated townhouse complex on 138 Street south of 66 Avenue (Charleston Green, 6537 138 St), and one membership complex at 15020 66A Ave (Sullivan Mews).

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in East Newton

items.t: City zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000: governs East Newton; MLS data for Chelsea Gardens records its zoning as RM45.

Plans: the East Newton North NCP was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update and East Newton South's land-use designations were superseded by that update, with the NCP still guiding public amenities and infrastructure — read the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000, not just the old NCP documents.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): Surrey allows a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; the BC Building Code permits one secondary suite per house. This applies to the detached streets around the 55+ complexes, not to the strata lots inside them.

Manufactured-home parks in Surrey carry a City policy layer on top of the provincial Act: the City's Manufactured Home Park Policy brochure tells park residents the property owner must give 12 months' notice of a final moving date, can only give that notice after receiving all permits and approvals, and must pay $20,000 on or before the move-out date. Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw, 2025, No. 21788 does NOT apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — park residents rely on the provincial Act and the City policy, not that bylaw.
Property taxes (city-wide, not area-specific): City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Newton

items.t: Chelsea Gardens is two addresses and two housing forms under one name. Apartment condos sit at 13870 70 Ave and ground-level townhouse-style homes at 13888 70 Ave, in one gated LMS1416 community — a buyer comparing two Chelsea Gardens listings may be comparing different building forms and fee schedules, not just different units.

The "55+" label on the King George Boulevard manufactured-home parks near East Newton does not hold up. Crispen Bays (7790 King George Blvd) and Crestway Bays (8220 King George Blvd) are listed by a park directory as all-ages, and Crestway listings call the park family-oriented — a buyer who assumes every Newton park is seniors-only will be wrong on these two.

Sullivan Mews' monthly fee is not a strata fee. Its listing states the $540 monthly amount covers taxes, heat, electricity, management, insurance and water because the purchase is a membership — comparing that figure line-by-line against a strata fee at Chelsea Gardens misleads. Listing-stated — confirm current amounts in the membership documents.

The retirement residence on 74 Avenue runs on a 65+ basis, not 55+. Building sources describe Arbourside Court as geared to adults 65 and older — a 58-year-old downsizer who qualifies for the strata complexes does not automatically qualify there.

The old East Newton plans are partly dead documents. The City states East Newton North was rescinded and East Newton South's designations were superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a seller quoting an old NCP density for a lot near these complexes is quoting a superseded plan.

Surrey's 2025 Tenant Protection Bylaw does not cover manufactured-home parks. Bylaw No. 21788, adopted for rental-building redevelopment, expressly does not apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — park residents' protection is the provincial 12-month notice and $20,000 compensation framework plus the City's Manufactured Home Park Policy.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in East Newton?
faq.a: Two strata complexes verified in this research — Chelsea Gardens (13870 / 13888 70 Ave, LMS1416) and Charleston Green (6537 138 St, NWS2625) — plus one non-strata option, Sullivan Mews (15020 66A Ave), where you buy a membership, not a strata lot.

faq.q: Why does Sullivan Mews say no mortgages are possible?
faq.a: Because, per its listing, it is not a strata — the purchase is a membership, so there is no strata title for a lender to register against, and the listing states a purchase must be cash. Confirm the current membership and financing terms in the membership documents before writing an offer.

faq.q: Is Arbourside Court something I can buy?
faq.a: No. Arbourside Court, 13751 74 Ave, is an independent retirement living residence with supportive services — its own site describes senior apartments with rents, operating since 2001. It is a place to rent with services, not strata ownership.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the 55+ complexes?
faq.a: It is complex-by-complex. MLS data for Chelsea Gardens records pets allowed with restrictions; Charleston Green listings state pets allowed; Sullivan Mews listings state 1 small pet and a maximum of 2 occupants. Confirm the specific pet bylaw in the Form B and registered bylaws.

faq.q: What transit can I use day to day from the 70 Avenue cluster?
faq.a: The R1 RapidBus on King George Boulevard links Newton Exchange and King George Station via Surrey Central Station for the Expo Line; there is no SkyTrain station in East Newton itself.

faq.q: Where is the closest urgent care?
faq.a: The Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 6830 King George Blvd, and Surrey Memorial Hospital is at 13750 96 Ave.
